newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas trades down but bids end steady to high.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas trades down but bids end steady to high.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract saw 125 lots traded in eight separate deals on Tuesday morning.
The total is higher than has recently been seen and follows an encouraging day's trade on Monday when 215 lots, again more than normal, were traded.

Deals were concentrated in only two months, July '97 and April '98, with four trades done in each case. Both ended the morning session lower, with July down to 10.260, off by 0.015 pence from Monday's settlement, while April was off by 0.15 pence to 12.10.
But these falls were against the trend.

Nine of the twelve contract months were bid at or above the previous day's settlement by the close, raising the possibility that trades will be done at higher levels when the market reopens for the afternoon session.
A physical trader said he was not aware of any unusual drivers behind the market on Tuesday morning, adding that activity on the OTC market had been quiet.
There was no further sign of unusual interest for prompt gas, as had been seen on the day-ahead market on Monday and which was caused by rumoured problems either at a beach terminal or offshore.
